summary: This bill requires the Attorney General to annually publish a list of licensed gun dealers that had 25 or more firearms traced to crimes within three years of sale in at least two of the prior three years, and bars all federal agencies from contracting with any dealer on that list (with a national security waiver option).

scores.thoughts: The bill imposes restrictions on federal contracting with certain firearms dealers but does not alter overall spending levels, appropriations, or budgets. It affects procurement eligibility rather than the amount of government expenditure.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, public coverage, or market-based healthcare systems.

The bill requires public listing of dealers with high volumes of short time-to-crime traces and bars federal agencies from contracting with them. This uses federal purchasing power to penalize dealers linked to rapid diversion of firearms into crime, constituting a moderate, indirect form of gun regulation aimed at reducing illegal trafficking.
No provisions relate to immigration pathways, border enforcement, or immigrant protections.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
While the bill allows a national-security waiver for DoD and DHS contracts, it does not change defense spending levels or authorize new military appropriations.
No provisions concern environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety-net benefits.
No provisions relate to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill uses crime-trace data but does not alter sentencing, policing practices, rehabilitation programs, or criminal procedure.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
No provisions concern deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal targets.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions relate to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
No provisions address worker protections, union rights, or employer obligations.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
